newsitem.title: INDIA: India's MRPL raises 7.26 bln in bonds.
newsitem.headline: India's MRPL raises 7.26 bln in bonds.

text.p: Indian refiner Mangalore Refineries and Petrochemicals Ltd (MRPL) raised 7.26 billion rupees through an issue of convertible bonds to its two major promoters - the Aditya Birla Group and Hindustan Petroluem Corporation Ltd, a company official said on Monday.
"We have completed the FCD (fully convertible debenture) issue to promoters," MRPL company secretary Vimal Kejriwal told Reuters on Monday.
The issue will part finance the company's plans to raise the refining capacity to nine million tonnes of crude oil a year from the current three million tonnes.
The expansion will cost 36.9 billion rupees, according the Industrial Credit and Investment Corp of India Ltd, a term-lending bank.
Kejriwal said the company has not yet taken a decision on a public issue of shares to part finance the expansion.
Analysts expect a large public offering of shares from the company later this year.
The terms of the conversion of the bonds into equity shares will be based on the prevailing guidelines, MRPL told an extraordinary meeting of shareholders in June which approved the issue.
"As a result of conversion of FCDs, the holding of the two promoting groups will increase to approximately 37.35 percent each (from 26 percent each now)," MRPL told shareholders.
